# kube-agents Build Review

_A grounded, reality-checked assessment of what was built, what genuinely works, what is honestly deferred, and exactly how to run and test it yourself._

Repository root: `/Users/adamparco/github/kube-agents` · Branch reviewed: `docs/design-end-state-specs` · All Phases 0–7 merged to `main`.

---

## 1. Executive summary

**What it is.** kube-agents is a Kubernetes-native system of **read-only AI operations agents** for GKE, organized as a **hub-and-spoke, three-tier hierarchy** (Platform → Cluster-Admin → Developer-Team). Each agent is a hardened pod reconciled from a single generic `Agent` custom resource (`kubeagents.x-k8s.io/v1alpha1`). Agents never mutate the cluster or cloud directly; the **only** write path is a GitOps pull request that a human approves and the customer's CI/CD applies (KCC YAML or Terraform HCL). A read-only ChatOps router (`kage-router`) is the front door; a controller-runtime operator renders and manages the workloads; admission policies (ValidatingAdmissionPolicies) and a hermetic review-gate scorer are the enforcement backstops.

**Scope delivered (Phases 0–7).** Foundations and the reference GitOps repo (P0); the read-only Platform Agent + GitOps loop and the generalized `Agent` CRD (P1); the Cluster-Admin Agent, `kage-router` deterministic routing, and the F4 provisioning cascade (P2); the Developer-Team Agent + namespace isolation proof (P3); coordination, OKF knowledge, and push-first triggers (P4); the security review gate + pod/RBAC hardening (P5); failure-isolation chaos suite (P6); and cloud-agnostic seams — KCC↔Terraform parity, a CircleCI second pipeline, and a provider-neutral observability/OTLP seam (P7).

**Honest verdict on maturity.** This is a **real system, well past prototype, sitting at the "production-architecture, pre-production-hardening" point on the spectrum.** The load-bearing security claims are not prose — they are enforced in Go, in CRD CEL, and in live admission policies, and they were **re-verified live against a running Kind cluster this review** (cardinality webhook, read-only RBAC VAP, pod-hardening VAP all denied/admitted with the exact expected policy messages). The operator builds, vets, and tests clean (controller at 88.6% coverage under envtest), and every hermetic parity/scorer suite passes. What keeps it short of "production-proven" is deliberate, disclosed deferral: no live second-cloud or scratch-GKE identity validation, egress enforcement proven only on Calico (not the default kindnet dev cluster), and a set of explicitly-scoped v1 non-goals (gVisor sandbox, per-request user down-scoping, cross-object attenuation webhook). Crucially, the audit found **no fabricated "works" claims** — every gap maps to a documented deferral or an honestly-rated `partial`.

## 2. Architecture at a glance

### Hub-and-spoke, three read-only tiers

| Tier               | Scope                         | Identity key `(tier, scope)`               | Provisions                         |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------- |
| **platform**       | project                       | `platform;project`                         | Cluster-Admin agents (F4 cascade)  |
| **cluster-admin**  | project + cluster             | `cluster-admin;project;cluster`            | Developer-Team agents (F4 cascade) |
| **developer-team** | project + cluster + namespace | `developer-team;project;cluster;namespace` | — (leaf)                           |

The `(tier, scope)` identity is derived by a **single source of truth**, `k8s-operator/internal/agentindex/identity.go`, and is consumed by **both** the cardinality webhook and the ChatOps router — so the uniqueness key and the routing key cannot drift. This was proven live: a duplicate-CR dry-run was rejected with a message printing exactly the `agentindex.Identity` output.

### The 5 load-bearing invariants

Stated verbatim from `docs/design/README.md` and mirrored into `.claude/harness/invariants.md`:

1. **Agents are read-only** on all cluster/cloud APIs; the only write path is a reviewed PR.
2. **All mutation flows through GitOps** — agent proposes → human approves → customer CI/CD applies KCC/Terraform. No direct `kubectl`/`gcloud` writes, no break-glass.
3. **Agents never call each other directly** — they coordinate only via shared state (the GitOps repo + OKF knowledge entries).
4. **Each tier is scope-bounded** (project / cluster / namespace) by a per-agent read-only identity, enforced by policy, not convention.
5. **Every change is reviewed, attributable, and revertible.**

### Controller / router / agents / GitOps flow

```
ChatOps turn ─▶ kage-router (read-only)
                 resolve (tier,scope) ─▶ authorize BEFORE dispatch ─▶ re-publish to target agent topic
                                                                              │
Agent pod (hardened, read-only) ◀────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   │  reads cluster/cloud (get/list/watch only) + OKF knowledge
   │  authors declarative artifacts (KCC YAML / Terraform HCL)
   ▼
git push + gh pr create (via credential-proxy sidecar) ─▶ GitOps repo PR
                                                              │  human review (CODEOWNERS) + review-gate scorer
                                                              ▼
                                    customer CI/CD (apply.yml / CircleCI) ─▶ kubectl / terraform apply
                                                              │
                                    VAP backstops reject any write-verb RBAC or un-hardened pod at admission
```

The **operator** (`k8s-operator/internal/controller`) renders a Deployment + 2 PVCs + 3 ConfigMaps + a Service per agent and **mints no RBAC and no ServiceAccount** — the read-only identity is pre-created via a GitOps RBAC overlay and enforced by `vap-agent-readonly`.

**Read-only posture is enforced by construction, not just intent:** the controller literally cannot mint agent RBAC (its ClusterRole has no RBAC verbs), and the renderer omits the `gke` MCP proxy (`container.googleapis.com`, exposes `create_cluster` etc.) entirely.

### 3.2 Router (`kage-router`)

**Purpose.** Resolve each inbound Google Chat turn to exactly one `(tier,scope)` agent, authorize the sender against **that target's** allowlist **before** dispatch (fail-closed), then re-publish to the target's Pub/Sub topic. Deterministic modes provably spend zero inference.

| Component                                                                       | Rating             | Evidence                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `internal/router/grammar.go` (slash/@handle grammar)                            | real-runnable      | Ordered tier-prefix table (canonical-before-alias), RFC1123 leaf validation; `canonical_beats_alias_prefix` subtest PASS                          |
| `internal/router/resolve.go` (deterministic core + inference boundary)          | real-runnable      | `inferenceCalls` atomic counter asserted **==0** across slash/handle/sticky matrices, **==1** only when model consulted                           |
| `internal/router/authorize.go` (before-dispatch allowlist)                      | real-runnable      | Three-rule fail-closed: empty sender deny, empty/absent allowlist deny-all, else membership; `mallory` refused, `alice` dispatched vs pstest fake |
| `internal/router/gateway.go` (enforces resolve→lookup→authorize→dispatch order) | real-runnable      | 9 test funcs; bind-thread only after authorized dispatch                                                                                          |
| `internal/router/pubsubinbound/` (Chat event parser + receiver)                 | real-runnable      | `TestReceiver_RoutesInboundEvents` PASS ~1.6s against in-process pstest                                                                           |
| `config/router/role.yaml` (get/list/watch on agents only)                       | real-static        | No write verbs — the ChatOps front door is itself read-only                                                                                       |
| `config/router/deployment.yaml` + `Dockerfile.router`                           | real-static        | Hardened distroless nonroot; **env placeholders** `REPLACE_WITH_PROJECT_ID` and **no Workload-Identity annotation**                               |
| NL inference (mode 3), sticky affinity, outbound replier                        | deferred-not-faked | Fully coded/tested with spy/fake but intentionally **unwired** in `cmd/router` (Phase-2 posture)                                                  |

Today's end-user behavior is **deterministic slash/@handle routing only** — NL inference is refused (`ErrInferenceUnavailable`), by design.

Both runtime-credential invariants were **confirmed**: skills open PRs and never mint privilege; the agent process never holds a write token (the sidecar does).

### 3.6 Observability

**Purpose.** Provider-neutral observability endpoints (Phase-7 goal: remove hard-wiring to GCP), with GCP/GKE as the zero-config default.

| Component                                                                                                        | Rating                       | Evidence                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `obs_backend.py` (per-signal base-URL selector)                                                                  | real-runnable                | Unset → exact googleapis hosts; per-signal override wins; non-gcp + missing URL → loud `SystemExit` (no silent GCP leak) |
| 5 query scripts (fetch_traces, analyze_trace_latency, get_chat_users, check_token_usage, get_metric_descriptors) | real-runnable (not run here) | Real `urllib` HTTP to Cloud Trace/Logging/Monitoring; need live GCP creds                                                |
| `deploy/shared/docker-entrypoint.sh` (OTLP endpoint seam)                                                        | real-runnable                | Baked GKE collector default; rewrites only when `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` set                                        |
| `observability-seam.py` (6 checks) + `otel-endpoint.sh` (6 checks)                                               | real-runnable                | **Both pass (exit 0) this review**                                                                                       |

Caveat: the endpoint is provider-neutral but **auth is not** — scripts always attach a `gcloud`/ADC bearer token, and **query translation** (MQL→PromQL, Cloud Trace→Tempo) is **deferred (D3)**. Pointing the URL at Prometheus/Tempo changes the host but not the request shape.

**One failed check, disclosed:** `gofmt -l .` flags **4 files** (`cmd/k8s-event-watcher/dedup.go`, `dispatcher_test.go`, `injector_test.go`, `watcher_test.go`) for the Go 1.19+ doc-comment list-indentation rule. `make build`/`make test` run `go fmt ./...` which silently rewrites them, **masking** that the committed source is not gofmt-clean. Cosmetic, not a correctness issue.

### 4.2 Re-verified **live on Kind this session** (adversarial audit)

The task premise "kind is not installed / no cluster" turned out **half-true**: the `kind` CLI is absent, but a fully-deployed Kind cluster (`kind-kube-agents-dev`, K8s **v1.31.2**, controller 1/1, both VAPs, 2 Agent CRs) was reachable. The following were **re-executed live** against it:

- **Cardinality webhook** — duplicate `cluster-admin-cluster-a` dry-run **rejected** with the exact `agentindex.Identity` key in the message.
- **`vap-agent-readonly`** — write-verb Role, impersonate ClusterRole, wrong-scope ClusterRole all **DENIED** by the policy message; read-only Role **ADMITTED**.
- **`vap-agent-pod-hardening`** — tier-labeled pod missing `readOnlyRootFilesystem` **DENIED** naming the field.

> Note: these live results depend on that cluster being up. On a fresh machine they require the setup in §6(b) before they can be re-run.

### 4.3 Verified previously (recorded in LEDGER), requires env rebuild to re-run

- Full `verify-phase2..7.sh` and `chaos-suite.sh` exit 0 on Kind (recorded 2026-07-24).
- Calico egress enforcement (`egress-enforcement.sh`) — proven on a Calico cluster (blocks off-allowlist IP, incl. metadata-server `169.254.169.254`).
- Live scratch-GKE platform GSA reconcile to viewer-only (7 roles, no clusterAdmin/admin).

| Scrubbing residual write-shaped prose from some `gke-*` skill docs       | phase-1 §Deferred                 | Does not breach runtime read-only ceiling; follow-on pass                  |

## 6. How to manually run & test it

### (a) Zero-setup / host-hermetic checks you can run RIGHT NOW

These need only `go`, `python3`, and `bash` — **no cluster, no docker, no cloud CLIs.** All verified green this review. Run from the repo root `/Users/adamparco/github/kube-agents`:

```bash
# 1) Operator build / vet / test (Go 1.26)
cd k8s-operator && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...
cd ..

# 2) Phase-7 hermetic parity + seam validators (all exit 0)
python3 dev/tests/iac-parity.py .
python3 dev/tests/circleci-parity.py .
python3 dev/tests/observability-seam.py .
bash   dev/tests/otel-endpoint.sh .

# 3) Review-gate scorer + extractor unit tests (40 tests OK)
python3 -m unittest scripts/review-gate/test_score_findings.py \
                    scripts/review-gate/test_extract_findings.py

# 4) Mutation-path invariant tests (hermetic, real local git repos)
cd dev && python3 -m unittest test_submit_suggestion test_detect_drift \
   test_read_knowledge test_raise_escalation test_heartbeat_sops
cd ..

# 5) Score a findings set by hand (proves the BLOCK rule)
echo '[{"agent":"rbac","findings":[{"message":"wildcard verb","file":"r.yaml","severity":"high"}]}]' \
  | python3 scripts/review-gate/score_findings.py --waivers security-review-waivers.yaml --today 2026-07-24 -
# → prints BLOCK, exits 1

# 6) Router determinism (inference_calls == 0)
cd k8s-operator && go test ./internal/router/ -run 'TestResolve|Inference|ThreadAffinity' -v
```

> `make test` runs `go fmt ./...` which will rewrite the 4 gofmt-dirty files listed in §4.1. If you want a clean tree, use `go test ./...` directly (no rewrite) or `git checkout` afterward.

### (b) Full inner loop on Kind

**Prerequisites — the ONLY genuinely missing binary is `kind`.** Everything else the suite truly needs (`go`, `docker`, `kubectl`, `python3`, `make`, `jq`, `bash`, `envsubst`) is present. `kustomize` is auto-bootstrapped by the operator Makefile via `go install`; `helm` is NOT used by the Kind loop (cert-manager is applied with `kubectl apply -f`); `terraform`/`circleci`/`yq` are never needed (parity is hermetic).

```bash
# 0) Install kind (the one blocker)
go install sigs.k8s.io/kind@latest        # or: brew install kind

# 1) Bring up the cluster (K8s v1.31.2, ctx kind-kube-agents-dev)
dev/cluster/up.sh

# 2) cert-manager (webhook TLS)
kubectl apply -f https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/releases/latest/download/cert-manager.yaml
kubectl -n cert-manager wait --for=condition=Available deploy --all --timeout=180s

# 3) Deploy YOUR LOCAL operator image — never the published v0.1.0.
#    `make deploy` does NOT build; it only sets the image + applies. So you must build +
#    kind-load a LOCAL tag first, then deploy THAT tag. (The published v0.1.0 is upstream's
#    binary, not your working tree; and it renders pods without readOnlyRootFilesystem, which
#    the hardening VAP rejects.) The helper does build → kind load → repoint in one step:
dev/cluster/reload-images.sh operator kind-kube-agents-dev
#    ...or longhand, if the controller Deployment doesn't exist yet:
#      make -C k8s-operator docker-build IMG=kube-agents/k8s-operator:dev
#      kind load docker-image kube-agents/k8s-operator:dev --name kube-agents-dev
#      cd k8s-operator && make deploy IMG=kube-agents/k8s-operator:dev && cd ..
kubectl apply -f examples/gitops-repo/policy/vap-agent-readonly.yaml

# 4) Run the per-phase gates
for p in 2 3 4 5 6 7; do dev/verify/verify-phase$p.sh kind-kube-agents-dev; done
```

**Stale-image rule (load-bearing).** Local images reuse a fixed tag (`:dev`, `:latest`) with `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent`, so a same-tag image is **not** auto-refreshed. A Kind gate can read green against a stale build that under-enforces an admission invariant. **Always rebuild → `kind load` → `rollout restart`/`set image` before trusting a gate** — `reload-images.sh` does exactly this. This matters most before Phase 6.

**Calico caveat for egress.** kindnet does **not** enforce NetworkPolicy, so on a kindnet cluster `egress-enforcement.sh` self-defers (exit 3, non-fatal). This used to require standing up a second, Calico-only cluster. It no longer does — `up.sh` builds the one inner-loop cluster with Calico already, so:

```bash
dev/cluster/up.sh                                         # 2 nodes, Calico, operator, VAP, agent images
dev/tests/egress-enforcement.sh kind-kube-agents-dev   # exit 0 = proven; exit 3 = deferred
```

No `calico`/`calicoctl` binary is needed — install is pure `kubectl apply`.

**Did this review test the _right_ image?** Yes for everything it actually asserted:

- **Controller + webhook + admission** — the live cluster's controller was a **local** build (`kube-agents/k8s-operator:dev`, rebuilt and re-verified this pass), so the webhook/reconciler/admission checks tested the **working tree**, not upstream's `ghcr.io/...:v0.1.0`.
- **VAPs (read-only RBAC, pod hardening)** — image-independent: they validate the real policy YAML at admission regardless of which operator image runs.
- **Go/envtest + hermetic Python/shell suites** — always compile and run the local source; no container image involved.
- **Agent _runtime content_** — **not exercised live** at all (needs inference creds; deferred). The running agent pods still carried the upstream `:v0.1.0` image, but pod hardening (`readOnlyRootFilesystem`, etc.) is rendered by the **local controller**, not baked into the agent image — so no wrong-image result was masked. To run agents from your working tree, `reload-images.sh agents …` and set `spec.deployment.imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent`.

The one trap to avoid: following the old INSTALL.md literally (`make deploy IMG=ghcr.io/...:v0.1.0` and stop) would have tested the **upstream** controller, not yours. That step is now fixed to build + load a local tag first.

## 7. Caveats, gotchas & known limitations

- **Stale-image rule** (most important): same `v0.1.0` tag + `IfNotPresent` means Kind will serve a stale build and can silently under-enforce. The published `v0.1.0` operator renders pods **without** `readOnlyRootFilesystem` — you must build+load a local image or Phase 6 fails. Always rebuild → `kind load` → restart before a gate.
- **`kubectl` `-gke` version gotcha**: the host `kubectl` is gcloud's `-gke` build, whose client `gitVersion` carries a `-gke` suffix. `verify-phase7.sh` correctly reads the **server-side** node `kubeletVersion` (not client version) to confirm a vanilla target — a robustness detail, not a gap.
- **kindnet vs Calico**: kindnet does not enforce NetworkPolicy; egress enforcement is proven only on a separate Calico cluster. On kindnet the netpol **shape** is validated structurally and enforcement self-defers (rc 3).
- **Missing CLIs → hermetic parity**: `terraform`, `circleci` (and `kind`/`calicoctl`) are absent; the Phase-7 IaC/pipeline claims are proven by stdlib-Python parity validators, with CLI-level validation explicitly deferred (D2/D4) — same honest pattern as Calico-for-kindnet.
- **Router in Kind is benign-CrashLoop**: `config/router/deployment.yaml` ships env placeholders (`REPLACE_WITH_PROJECT_ID`, `REPLACE_WITH_INBOUND_SUBSCRIPTION`) and the router SA has **no Workload-Identity annotation**, so `kage-router` cannot authenticate to real Pub/Sub in Kind and will crashloop — expected/benign until those are wired for a real project. The router's logic is proven hermetically against the pstest fake.
- **gofmt not clean**: 4 files fail `gofmt -l`; `make` masks it via `go fmt ./...`.
- **Image tag mismatch**: root `Makefile` tags agent images `:latest`; operator defaults + verify expect `:v0.1.0` — build/tag `:v0.1.0` explicitly.
- **`spec.iac.format` has zero Go consumers** — stored + schema-validated, not yet acted upon (rated `partial`, correctly).
- **Mutating `Default()` is an empty stub**; defaulting is via CRD markers.
- **Orphaned fixtures**: `examples/gitops-repo/policy/tests/*.yaml` cite a nonexistent `tests/e2e/vap_negative_test.sh`; the live VAP negatives use inline heredocs in `negative-attenuation.sh` instead.
- **Hygiene nits**: a ~66 MB untracked build artifact `k8s-operator/router` sits in the working tree (should be gitignored); `hack/ci-connection-test.sh` is unwired scaffolding; `k8s-operator/examples/agent.yaml` uses stale inline `slack.botToken` fields vs the CRD's `botTokenSecretRef` (latent — `slack.enabled: false`).
- **Docs naming**: `docs/design/` (numbered end-state specs 01–08) vs `docs/designs/` (detailed feature designs) are two intentional siblings, not a duplicate.
- **LEDGER is stale but UNDER-reports**: it says Phase 7 "auto-merge pending" while `main` is far past it — it under-claims, so it is not fabricating green results.

## 8. Bottom line

kube-agents is a **genuine, coherent, security-first system** — not a demo. The operator, router, webhooks, and identity model are real Go that builds, vets, and tests clean (88.6% controller coverage under envtest), and the central "agents are read-only" invariant is enforced at **three independent layers** — Go rendering (drops the mutating MCP, mints no RBAC), CRD CEL, and live ValidatingAdmissionPolicies — all of which were re-verified **live against a running Kind cluster this review** with the exact expected denial messages. The GitOps-only write path, fail-closed before-dispatch authorization, deterministic zero-inference routing, and the hermetic review-gate scorer are all code-backed and test-proven.

The honesty of the build is its most notable property: **no fabricated "works" claims were found.** Every gap is a disclosed, gated-off deferral (second cloud, scratch-GKE identity, gVisor, per-request down-scoping, cross-object attenuation) or an accurately-rated `partial` (`spec.iac.format`, `parentRef` cross-object checks). The remaining work to reach "production-proven" is exactly the deferred cloud/live legs plus minor hygiene (gofmt, image tagging, orphaned fixtures, the untracked binary) — nothing that undermines the architecture.

**Where it sits:** a real, well-architected, thoroughly self-tested v1 whose security backbone is live-verified, awaiting cloud-scale and second-cloud validation before it can be called production-hardened. For a reviewer on their own machine, the entire hermetic surface (Go suite, parity/seam validators, review-gate scorer, mutation-path tests) runs green with zero setup today; the full live loop needs only `kind` installed plus the documented rebuild-and-load discipline.
